answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces quadratic cryptographic stake burning for identity registration. Minting each identity requires burning base-token reserves, scaling cost superlinearly as $C(n) \propto n^2$. Like a rising tide submerging cheap replicas, an attacker attempting to amass identities on an isolated knoll faces explosive economic friction. Even minting a single fake agent costs more than its weight in raw copper.
